lines: 一只椋鸟，看不见整个鸟群，|它只盯着身边的六七只同伴。
A single starling can't see the flock.|It only watches the six or seven birds beside it.
可几十万只这样的鸟聚在一起，|就能在天上画出这样的形状。
Yet put a few hundred thousand of them together,|and they paint shapes like this across the sky.
没有领头鸟，也没有指挥。|1986 年，有人只用三条规则，|就在电脑里复现了这一幕。
No leader, no conductor.|In 1986, someone used just three rules|to recreate it on a computer.
这一期，我们从一只鸟出发，一路演进到六万只。
This episode, we start from one bird and evolve all the way to sixty thousand.
他叫克雷格·雷诺兹，|他把模拟出来的鸟叫作 Boids，“类鸟体”。
His name is Craig Reynolds.|He called his simulated birds boids: bird-oid objects.
每只 boid 只感知身边一小圈邻居，|只做三件事：
Each boid senses only the neighbors in a small radius,|and does just three things:
分离，离得太近就躲开；
separation: steer away when someone gets too close;
对齐，方向跟邻居保持一致；
alignment: match your neighbors' heading;
聚合，朝邻居的中心靠拢。
cohesion: move toward their center.
三股力相加，就是这一帧的转向。|没有全局规划，鸟群自己出现了。
Add the three forces, and that's this frame's steering.|No global plan, yet the flock simply emerges.
1992 年，它登上了《蝙蝠侠归来》，|生成了成群的蝙蝠和企鹅大军。
In 1992 it reached Batman Returns,|driving swarms of bats and an army of penguins.
1999 年的 GDC 上，|雷诺兹把它扩展成一整套转向行为：|寻找、逃离、徘徊、避障。
At GDC 1999,|Reynolds expanded it into a whole toolkit of steering behaviors:|seek, flee, wander, avoid.
核心只有一行：期望速度，减去当前速度。
The core is a single line: desired velocity minus current velocity.
放进一只鹰，每只鸟多一条“逃离”，|鸟群就会被撕开，再重新合拢。
Drop in a hawk and give each bird one extra flee rule,|and the flock tears open, then closes again.
《半条命》里的异星飞鸟，|名字就直接叫 Boid。
In Half-Life, the alien flyers of Xen|are literally named Boid.
但这里藏着一个规模问题：|每只鸟都得先找出，谁是它的邻居。
But a scaling problem hides here:|every bird first has to find out who its neighbors are.
和所有鸟逐一比距离，|一千只鸟，每帧就是一百万次；|数量翻十倍，开销翻一百倍。
Compare against every other bird,|and a thousand birds cost a million checks per frame;|ten times the birds, a hundred times the cost.
解法是空间网格：每只鸟只查自己和相邻的格子，|开销从 n 的平方，降到接近 n。
The fix is a spatial grid: each bird checks only its own cell and the cells next to it,|and the cost drops from n squared to roughly n.
2006 年，雷诺兹靠它在 PS3 上，|跑起了一万五千个个体，每秒六十帧。
In 2006, Reynolds used it to run|fifteen thousand agents on a PS3 at sixty frames per second.
那真实的椋鸟看多远？|2008 年，STARFLAG 团队|重建了鸟群里每只鸟的三维位置。
So how far does a real starling look?|In 2008, the STARFLAG team|rebuilt the 3D position of every bird in a flock.
答案是：不按距离，|只看最近的六七只，不管它们离得多远。
The answer: not by distance.|Each bird tracks its six or seven nearest, however far away.
这叫拓扑邻居。|论文的模拟显示：密度剧变时，|这样的鸟群更不容易散。
These are topological neighbors.|The paper's simulations show that when density swings,|such flocks are harder to break apart.
再往上，就得交给 GPU：|每只鸟的位置和速度，存成浮点纹理里的一个像素。
Beyond that, hand it to the GPU:|each bird's position and velocity is one pixel of a float texture.
邻居也不再一个个去数，|先把所有鸟累加进一张网格，|记下每格的数量、中心和平均速度。
Neighbors are no longer counted one by one;|every bird is splatted into a grid|that keeps each cell's count, center and average velocity.
每只鸟只读周围的格子，|三条规则，就变成了对一张场的采样。
Each bird reads only the cells around it,|and the three rules become samples of a field.
六万五千五百三十六只，|每一只都在实时做着同样的三件事。
Sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six birds,|each doing the same three things, in real time.
从三条规则到六万只，规则几乎没变，|变的是我们怎么组织数据。
From three rules to sixty thousand birds, the rules barely changed.|What changed is how we organize the data.
可如果每一只不再是一个点，|而是一条有骨骼、会摆尾的鱼呢？
But what if each one isn't a point anymore,|but a fish with a skeleton and a swinging tail?

credit: GDC 2017 · Matt Nava · Creating the Art of ABZÛ
lines: 每条鱼大概有 60 到 100 个关节
there's like 60 to 100 joints
每一帧，你都得把每条鱼的关节全部更新一遍
and every frame you have to update all of those joints per fish
所以要更新的不只是一万条鱼
so instead of just having 10,000 fish to update
而是一万乘以一百个关节，这太疯狂了
you have ten thousand times 100 joints, which is crazy
下一期，我们潜进《ABZÛ》的海底，|看上万条鱼怎么游出生命感。
Next time, we dive into the sea of ABZÛ|to see how ten thousand fish come alive.
而这一切，还得从一只鸟说起。
And all of it starts, once again, with a single bird.
